- Overestimate prices when sentiment is negative (especially strong negative sentiment), especially in early forecast windows.  
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is mildly positive or neutral, particularly after recent price spikes.  
- Overshoot after sharp upward sentiment spikes; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% in subsequent periods.  
- Mean-revert forecasts when sentiment is consistently negative over 3+ days; adjust downward by 1–3% per day.  
- Lagged price movements (e.g., 1–2 day delay) are overestimated in short-term forecasts; apply a 0.5–1.0% downward correction for 1–3 day horizons.  
- Avoid overconfidence in 30-day forecasts when sentiment is volatile; reduce forecast variance by 15–20% in high-sentiment volatility windows.
